name: Jediael
overview: Jediael was a male figure identified in the Scriptures as the son of Shimri. Beyond this direct paternal link, the biblical record does not provide further details about his tribe or additional personal notes. His mention in 1 Chronicles 11:45 situates him within the genealogical and historical context of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jediael means 'known of God [El],' reflecting a recognition or relationship with the Lord. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 11:45, underscores the theocentric nature of biblical naming practices, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Jediael as the son of Shimri. It is also inferred that he had a brother named Joha, suggesting a family unit mentioned within the same passage. No other family relationships are recorded for him beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Jediael's significance lies primarily in his inclusion in the genealogical records of Israel, demonstrating the faithfulness of God in preserving His people through generations. His identification as the son of Shimri connects him to the broader narrative of the community of God's people as recorded in 1 Chronicles. Though not a central figure in major biblical events, his mention affirms the detailed care with which Scripture preserves the lineage of those known to God.
